subject: Re: Long-context evals and model recommendations (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed next steps — long-context evals

Hey Jane / Tom — thanks again for the discovery today, really helpful to see the workloads and constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear plan: 

Recap of needs:
- Ingest and summarize multi-page contracts and compliance bundles (typical doc = 20–80 pages, up to ~50k tokens).
- Must preserve factual accuracy for clause-level summaries and redlines; minimize hallucinations on obligations and dates.
- Latency target for on-demand summarization: < 1s ideal, up to 2s tolerated for very long documents.
- Cost sensitivity: you prefer a balanced approach (start with a higher-fidelity configuration for eval, then optimize).
- Data requirements: PII redaction and retention policy (you mentioned 90 days staging retention).

Proposed evaluation plan (what Redwood recommends to validate fit):
1) Run a long-context eval across 3 model/config variants using your sample set:
   - redwood-longcontext-v2 (our long-window tuned model; higher fidelity, optimized KV cache)
   - open-llama-70b-lc-q8 (open 3rd-party long-window baseline, quantized)
   - redwood-cost-optimized-3q (lower-cost variant to test cost/latency tradeoffs)

2) Benchmarks we'll produce for each run:
   - Summarization fidelity (rouge/bleu + human eval on 50 seed contracts)
   - Truncation behavior: where the model drops content (token offsets) and effect on key-clause recall
   - Latency and per-token cost (median / p95) under your target batch sizes
   - Hallucination/regression checks on dates, obligations, and party names

3) Deliverables (expected 7–10 business days after we receive sample data):
   - Eval reports (PDF) with charts and per-model tradeoffs
   - Prompt set used (JSONL) and the seed prompts for contract extractive + abstractive summaries
   - Tooling notes for integrating prefix/KV caching to maintain fidelity across multi-step summarization

Immediate asks from your side:
- Share a representative sample (20–50 docs). If any contain sensitive PII, please mark and we can run redaction first.
- Confirm if we can stage data in our secure eval environment (S3 w/ customer-segregated bucket, 90d retention) or if you require on-prem testing.

Attached: prompt-set-contract-summary-v1.jsonl (seed prompts) and a short benchmark primer (redwood-long-context-eval-benchmarks.pdf).

If that plan looks good I’ll queue it with our inference team and target a first-pass report in ~1 week after samples arrive. I can also loop in Product/Runtime (cc’d Michael & Dev) if you want specific kernel/quantization details.

Thanks — Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) For truncation behavior testing, can you confirm whether Redwood will return token-level offsets to help us map back into source documents? We need that for traceability.
2) For PII redaction: we can do a first pass on our side but would prefer Redwood to run a redaction step in the eval pipeline as an extra safeguard. Is that supported?
3) Any NDA / data processing addendum we should sign before you pull samples into your staging bucket?

We’ll compile a representative set — I can share a 20-doc sample by EOD Monday. Attaching an example export (acme_contracts_sample_20.jsonl) to start.

Thanks,

Thanks Jane — answers inline and next steps.

On 2026-03-03 17:05, Jane Porter wrote:
> 1) For truncation behavior testing, can you confirm whether Redwood will return token-level offsets to help us map back into source documents? We need that for traceability.

Yes — our eval pipeline can return token offsets and a simple mapping of output spans to input token indices. We’ll include a CSV that lists: doc_id, model, prompt_variant, truncated (bool), truncation_token_index_start, truncation_token_index_end. That should let you tie summaries back to the source.

> 2) For PII redaction: we can do a first pass on our side but would prefer Redwood to run a redaction step in the eval pipeline as an extra safeguard. Is that supported?

We support a pre-processing redaction pass (pattern- and ML-based) as part of the eval pipeline. It’s configurable — if you’d like, we can run both: you do a first-pass, we run a second-pass and provide a diff of redacted spans.

> 3) Any NDA / data processing addendum we should sign before you pull samples into your staging bucket?

We have a standard DPA/MFA that covers staging eval data; I’ll send a link to the DPA and our secure upload instructions (short DocuSign + S3 presigned upload). If you need on-prem testing we can also ship our private eval runner under an SOW.

Next steps: 
- We’ll queue the eval once you confirm DPA and upload the sample (link below).
- Michael / Dev — can you confirm capacity for a priority eval slot next week? Target: 7 business days to first-pass report after samples landed.

Links: 
- DPA & upload instructions: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyZ-long-context-evals
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/ACME-001

Thanks — I’ll stand by for the sample and DPA confirmation.

— Marissa
